source.title: Assessment of neural network augmented Reynolds averaged Navier Stokes turbulence model in extrapolation modes
source.authors: S. Bhushan; G. Burgreen; Wesley Brewer; I. Dettwiller

record.tranche_reason: Tests how mini-batch size affects overfitting and model accuracy in a neural turbulence model, extending batch-size findings to CFD regression.
record.gate_note: The study tests batch-size effects on training and validation residuals and a priori prediction accuracy. Its subject is a turbulence-production model, not a classifier trained on natural labels; it does not test whether networks that fit random labels generalize. Dropout is described but not varied.
record.test_reason: The study measures batch-size effects in turbulence regression, rather than the image classifiers or language models named in V5. Its a priori accuracy evaluation includes Hill data used in training, and the text does not establish a common fixed epoch budget for the batch sweep. These results do not test V5's held-out-performance claim or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' batch-size conclusion: the preferred batch size depends on network size, with overfitting below the optimum and reduced accuracy above it. Their broader conclusion is that full extrapolation performs poorly, while including target-flow data improves predictions and can enhance RANS turbulence predictions.
record.recipe_differences: Neural regression for turbulence production trained on DNS/LES flow data; mini-batch study is conducted in interpolation mode and evaluates a priori prediction accuracy, not classification test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Network size changes the optimal mini-batch size; smaller batches increase overfitting in the reported comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: In turbulence regression, smaller batches lower training residual but can raise validation residual; five-layer accuracy reaches R² = 0.8 at batch size 2K. Six- and seven-layer predictions show no significant improvement from 15K to 5K. The authors report a network-dependent optimal batch size and deteriorating accuracy above it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects fitting and interpolation accuracy in neural turbulence regression, with the preferred batch size depending on network architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: The full-extrapolation turbulence model has less than 5% a priori correlation with Hill DNS data; including Hill examples during training substantially improves prediction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coverage of the target flow regime in training strongly affects neural turbulence-model prediction under distribution shift.

record.peer_reviewed: The Physics of Fluids (venue stated in study metadata)
record.problems: The batch-size comparisons are in interpolation mode on a turbulence-production regression task, not the image or language settings in V5. Exact batch-specific accuracy values are largely conveyed in figures; the text provides qualitative comparisons and one R2 value.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible batch-size results beyond R1–R5. The text also reports the six-layer 5K batch as optimal and describes broader comparisons in Fig. 10; these are represented in the row conditions and notes rather than as extra rows because no separate outcome value is stated for each comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width increases beyond zero training error and their effect on test error; the depth comparisons do not establish an interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets. An adaptive learning-rate schedule is not this comparison.
Held-out performance of image classifiers or language models under fixed epoch budgets, including recipe adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout's effect on held-out error. The reported batch and architecture experiments use 20% dropout without a dropout comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Influence-defined memorized-example removal versus equal-sized random removal. Data clustering does not test this.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Keskar et al. for large-batch deterioration and Srivastava et al. for dropout, but neither citation establishes a test of a listed version. The supplied Figure 10 text does not preserve plotted values sufficiently to reconstruct additional numerical comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Widening beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Fixed-epoch comparisons in image classification and language modeling; adaptations such as longer training, warmup, normalization, or regularization.
Dropout was not varied in the reported experiments.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Mini-batch sweeps for the Hill turbulence-production model
reader_labels.reason: The study reports overfitting with smaller-than-optimal batches and reduced accuracy with larger-than-optimal batches, while the batch size giving best performance depends on network size (R1–R5).
